117740.name: Lubavitch of Wisconsin
117740.note: Wisconsin Jewish Chronicle (7 July 2019): 'Shmotkin brought the Chabad movement to Wisconsin back in October of 1968.' JTA Daily Bulletin (25 Nov 1968, 'Lubavitcher Movement Opens Wisconsin Regional Office'): 'The Lubavitcher movement has announced the opening of a new regional office in Milwaukee, Wis., Its seventh in the United States', headed by Rabbi Israel Shmotkin. Lubavitch News Service (30 Aug 1973, reprinted on lubavitch.com 7 Aug 2009): the new headquarters 'is a spacious 3 story, 33 room mansion, located at 3109 North Lake Drive, in Milwaukee', where it still is; where the office was in 1968-73 is not stated.

117738.name: Chabad Madison
117738.note: Lubavitch.com (28 July 2015, 'In The Footsteps of Their Parents'), Faygie and Yona Matusof: 'When we arrived in 1980, we were told that it's only a matter of time before we leave.' Lubavitch.com (2025, 'Chabad of Madison Unveils New Center'): 'Founded in 1980 by Rabbi Yona and Faygie Matusof, Chabad of Madison started out serving Jewish students in the University of Wisconsin.' Wisconsin Jewish Chronicle (undated, filed 31 March 2008, 'mark 25 years'): 'They married in August 1980, seven weeks before they moved to Madison.' Medium, not high: there was Chabad in Madison before them. The Daily Cardinal (24 Feb 2006): 'The international organization first appeared at UW-Madison in 1972'; the Chronicle (7 July 2019): 'In 1970, Lubavitch of Wisconsin was operating out of fewer than a half-dozen outposts, including Chabad of the East Side and Madison Chabad House.' Who ran it then is not found. Homes (2025 article): 'a small Chabad House on the ground floor of their home', then the Regent Street Chabad House (the Daily Cardinal: Chabad 'moved to Regent Street' in the early '80s), then 1711 Monroe St (property found in 2020; grand opening April 27, 2025).

earlier.where: the ground floor of the Matusofs' home
the Chabad House on Regent Street

119680.name: Mikvah Chaya Moussia
119680.note: No year found for the mikvah of Chabad Madison (Mrs. Faygie Matusof; 225 Campbell Street). Lubavitch.com (28 July 2015) lists 'services and a mikveh' among what the Matusofs (arrived 1980) built. Its chabad.org listing is in the first online directory (listings published July 22 2004), so it existed by then.

304247.name: Chabad at the University of Wisconsin
304247.note: UW-Madison interfaith staff page: 'In 2005, he and his wife Henya moved back to Madison to direct the Chabad activities on the UW campus.' Lubavitch.com (28 July 2015): 'In 2005, the young couple took the reins of Chabad on campus at University of Wisconsin-Madison'. The Daily Cardinal (24 Feb 2006): 'since September it has grown from having a few students attend Friday-night dinners to over 30', at 'their home on West Gilman Street'. Its chabad.org listing went up Aug 22 2005. Now 223 W. Gilman Street.

earlier.where: the Matusofs' home on West Gilman Street

1792807.name: YJP - Young Jewish Professionals - Madison
1792807.note: Lubavitch.com (28 July 2015): Rabbi Yona and Faygie Matusof's son Avremel 'joined his parents four years ago to expand programming for young Jewish professionals' (count back: 2011). Its chabad.org listing went up March 6 2012. Medium: counted back.

117739.name: Chabad of Downtown
117739.note: Wisconsin Jewish Chronicle (17 Feb 2009, 'Peltz Center to honor Samuels couple on 30 years'): 'when Shmotkin asked Samuels to come to Milwaukee in 1980, the Rebbe gave his blessing. At first, Samuels was education director and taught at a community high school that didn't last. In 1990, he opened Chabad of Downtown'. Rabbi Yoseph and Chashy Samuels; now 1301 N Astor Street.

315558.name: Chabad of the East Side
315558.note: No start date found. Wisconsin Jewish Chronicle (about June 2004, filed 31 March 2008, 'Ten years after Rebbe's passing'): 'Lubavitch of Wisconsin now has centers downtown, on the East Side, in Bayside and Mequon', with 'The Shul-East' and Rabbi Yerachmiel Kittner. The Chronicle (7 July 2019) also names 'Chabad of the East Side' among the outposts of 1970, which is not confirmed. Rabbi Yisroel and Mushka Lein lead it now; the Chronicle (6 March 2019): they 'moved from New York to Milwaukee more than six years ago'. Now 3030 East Kenwood Boulevard; its chabad.org listing went up Sept 23 2005.

117920.name: Jewish Reach - Russian Education & Aid Center
117920.note: Wisconsin Jewish Chronicle (undated, filed 31 March 2008, 'Rabbis reach out to next generation of FSU Jews'): Rabbi Yaacov Elman, 'director of Jewish REACH Synagogue for Russian Jews at 3510 N. Oakland Ave.', 'has served as a spiritual leader to the Russian-speaking Jews of Milwaukee in a program underwritten by Lubavitch of Wisconsin since 1991.' IRS: Jewish Reach Inc, ruling Jan 1994.

119683.name: Jewish Beginnings - Lubavitch Preschool
119683.note: Chinuch Office directory of Chabad schools (2023-24): Jewish Beginnings Lubavitch Preschool, 6401 N. Santa Monica Blvd., 'Founded: 1975'. Not confirmed elsewhere; the Wisconsin Jewish Chronicle (27 Aug 2018): 'The school's first accreditation from the nonprofit was in 1998.' IRS: Jewish Beginnings Lubavitch Preschool Inc, ruling May 1993. Medium: one list.

316577.name: Bader Hillel Academy
316577.note: An older school that Lubavitch took over. Wisconsin Jewish Chronicle (undated, filed 31 March 2008, 'Lubavitch to administer Hillel Academy'; it gives the federation's allocation 'for fiscal year 2004-2005' and 'the new school year begins on Sept. 1', so summer 2004): 'Beginning this school year, Lubavitch of Wisconsin will take over the management of the school'; B. Devorah Shmotkin, 'director of the Children's Lubavitch Living and Learning Center, will be the school's principal'. The school itself: 'Since its founding in 1960, Bader Hillel Academy has served as a cornerstone of Jewish education in Milwaukee' (its site, baderhillel.org); the Chronicle (2 Sept 2011) on its 50th anniversary. Medium: the article's date is inferred, and the Chinuch Office directory (2023-24) gives 'Founded: 1996'. Its chabad.org listing went up Sept 27 2005, at the preschool's address (6401 N Santa Monica Blvd).

150714.name: The Shul
150714.note: No start date found for The Shul (Congregation Ahavat Yisrael, Bayside), Rabbi Shmaya Shmotkin's. Wisconsin Jewish Chronicle (31 Jan 2010): Jeff Langer 'has been a member of Congregation Ahavat Yisrael' for 'about 10 years' (so it existed by about 2000), and it had moved 'four or five times'. The Chronicle (undated, filed 31 March 2008, 'Handy volunteers'): 'The Shul actually began in the basement of Shmotkin's Bayside home, and then rented the Bayside Community Center every week'; 'About two years ago, it began renting two non-adjoining spaces' at the Audubon Court shopping center. On Dec. 17 (2009) the Bayside village board approved its move into the former Pandl's in Bayside restaurant, now 8825 N Lake Dr.

earlier.where: the basement of Rabbi Shmaya Shmotkin's Bayside home

213095.name: The Peltz Center for Jewish Life
213095.note: Wisconsin Jewish Chronicle (11 June 2008): 'The Peltz Center will be concluding the 25th year since Fagie and Rabbi Dovid Rapoport established themselves in Milwaukee', marked June 25 2008; the 'then-Chabad of the North Shore, which at first met in the basement of the rabbi's Fox Point house'; 'it took only about five years before Chabad of the North Shore outgrew the Fox Point house', so it bought 10 acres in Mequon; 'In 1994, Chabad of the North Shore merged with the old Congregation Agudas Achim, then-based on Milwaukee's West Side, and became Congregation Agudas Achim Chabad.' Lubavitch.com (17 Oct 2004): 'In 1988, when Lubavitch of Wisconsin bought the present property, they moved to Mequon'. Now 2233 West Mequon Road.

earlier.where: the basement of Rabbi Dovid Rapoport's Fox Point house (Chabad of the North Shore)

213104.name: Mequon Jewish Preschool
213104.note: No start date found. Wisconsin Jewish Chronicle (11 June 2008): Rivkie and Rabbi Motty Spalter were honored for their '20 years of dedication and hard work' for the Peltz Center, 'which among other things included founding what is now the Mequon Jewish Preschool', so after about 1988. The Chinuch Office directory (2023-24) gives 'Founded: 1969', before Chabad came to Wisconsin (1968) and to the North Shore (1983), so not used. Its chabad.org listing went up Oct 14 2004. Now 11112 Crown Court.

540234.name: Chabad of Kenosha
540234.note: Wisconsin Jewish Chronicle (30 April 2008): Rabbi Tzali Wilschanski, 'spiritual leader of the shul since September 2007', of Congregation B'nei Tzedek Chabad in Kenosha. Its chabad.org listing went up Aug 15 2007. IRS: Chabad Lubavitch of Kenosha Inc, ruling Sept 2010. Now 6520 67th Street.

768432.name: Friendship Circle
768432.note: Wisconsin Jewish Chronicle (undated, filed 31 March 2008, 'Special needs children, volunteers both enjoy new Friendship Circle'): 'a new Lubavitch of Wisconsin program, the Friendship Circle, which began this past summer.' The Chronicle's 'Ten years after Rebbe's passing' (about June 2004) already calls it Lubavitch's 'new youth volunteer program', so the summer is 2003 (or, at the latest, 2004). Medium: the article is undated. Rabbi Levi Stein runs it now; the Chronicle (5 Sept 2025): 'When Rabbi Levi Stein started operating Friendship Circle of Wisconsin in 2017'. IRS: The Friendship Circle Inc, Fox Point, ruling Aug 1995 (unexplained). Its chabad.org listing went up Nov 18 2008. Now 8649 N Port Washington Road.

1113327.name: Chabad of the Bay Area
1113327.note: Wisconsin Jewish Chronicle (23 Dec 2020): Rabbi Michoel Feinstein and his wife Esther 'moved to Green Bay in 2010'. Its chabad.org listing went up Feb 3 2010. The Chronicle (25 Nov 2013): a new home in 'a former church' being converted for Chabad of the Bay Area, now 3607 Libal Street.

1471811.name: Rohr Chabad Jewish Student Center
1471811.note: No start date found for Chabad at UW-Milwaukee. Wisconsin Jewish Chronicle (29 March 2012): 'Rabbi Yecheskel Thaler (director of UWM Chabad on Campus)'. Its chabad.org listing went up March 21 2011, so it existed by then. IRS: Chabad Lubavitch of UWM Inc, ruling Oct 2014. Rabbi Lev and Talia Voskoboynik lead it now; their site (chabadoncampusmke.com): 'In 2024, after gaining experience serving at the Chabad at the University of Kansas, we moved from Lawrence, Kansas to Milwaukee'. Now 3054 N Hackett Avenue.

1899937.name: Chabad of Waukesha - Brookfield
1899937.note: Wisconsin Jewish Chronicle (30 Jan 2013): Rabbi Levi and Rebbetzin Fraidy Brook 'on Dec. 14 closed on a facility in Waukesha that is the new headquarters of Chabad of Waukesha. This latest affiliate of Lubavitch of Wisconsin opened this past summer.' The Chronicle (3 Nov 2020): Chabad of Waukesha-Brookfield, 'which first opened to the public in 2012', moved out of the rabbi's house to 1275 N. Barker Road in Brookfield. Its chabad.org listing went up July 5 2012.

earlier.where: a facility in Waukesha bought Dec. 14, 2012 (in 2020 the Chronicle calls the old space the rabbi's house)

2236192.name: Bader Hillel High
2236192.note: Wisconsin Jewish Chronicle (1 Aug 2013): 'The new school is Hillel High School, a day school under the auspices of Lubavitch of Wisconsin that is scheduled to start classes Thursday, Aug. 22. The school will meet in a former office building at 2629 N. Downer Ave. in Milwaukee.' The Chinuch Office directory (2023-24): 'Founded: 2013'. Its chabad.org listing went up May 29 2013. Now 6789 N Green Bay Avenue, Glendale.

earlier.where: a former office building at 2629 N. Downer Ave., Milwaukee

2901465.name: Chabad of Glendale
2901465.note: No start date found: Rabbi Mendel Shmotkin's 'Chabad of Glendale & River Hills' (its site, read through Firecrawl, gives no year; the Wisconsin Jewish Chronicle has no opening story). Its chabad.org listing went up March 26 2015, so it existed by then. IRS: Chabad Of Glendale Inc, ruling April 2018. Now 6791 N Green Bay Ave.

4441729.name: Ovation Senior Home
4441729.note: Rabbi Levi Emmer at Ovation (the old Jewish Home and Care Center, 1414 N Prospect Avenue; the home itself dates from 1906). No start date found. Wisconsin Jewish Chronicle (30 May 2012): 'Rabbi Levi Emmer of the Jewish Home and Care Center', so he was there by then; the Chronicle (1 Aug 2013): 'Rabbi Levi Emmer is the JHCC Director of Traditions and Spiritual Life'. Its chabad.org listing went up July 23 2019.

6490794.name: Chabad of Wauwatosa
6490794.note: No start date found: Rabbi Levi Shmotkin's Chabad of Tosa (its site gives no year; no news found). Its chabad.org listing went up Aug 5 2024, so it existed by then. IRS: Chabad Lubavitch Of Wauwatosa Inc, ruling April 2025.

7429629.name: Chabad Lubavitch Bay View
7429629.note: No start date found: Rabbi Yisroel Bresinger's center for Bay View, Milwaukee (the listing gives Lubavitch of Wisconsin's Glendale address, 6789 N. Green Bay Ave). IRS: Chabad Lubavitch Of Bay View Inc, ruling July 2026. Its chabad.org listing went up Sept 9 2026, so it existed by then.
